newsitem.title: UK: World wheat imports to rise in 97/98 - IGC.
newsitem.headline: World wheat imports to rise in 97/98 - IGC.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday estimated world wheat imports in 1997-98 would rise to 94.0 million tonnes from 1996-97 imports of 90.7 million.
Much of the rise was accounted for by an increase in estimated imports by China to 7.0 million tonnes from the 1996-97 estimate of 4.0 million tonnes.
This figure, however, was still well down on China's 1995-96 imports of 12.6 million tonnes.
A rise was seen in imports by North African countries to 6.9 million tonnes from the previous year's 6.0 million. This estimate excludes Egypt, which is counted seperately.
The figure was also pumped up by a rise in imports by unspecified countries to 2.5 million from the previous year's 1.3 million.
Iran's imports were seen cut to 3.8 million tonnes from the previous year's 5.0 million tonnes.
